Subject: Strict BYO lifecycle and egress minimization review

Hi Karthik / team,

Thanks for taking this on. Attached is a short set of BYO (Bring-Your-Own-Key) requirements we discussed during procurement. High-level asks from Acme security:

- Keys must remain customer-owned and never persist in vendor-controlled HSMs in clear form.
- Remote operator access should be zero-trust and auditable; emergency operator flows must be explicit with tokenized, short-lived credentials.
- Network egress from the on-prem environment must be limited to the control-plane endpoint and a small set of telemetry sinks.
- Rotation windows: monthly for ephemeral session wrapping keys; quarterly for KEKs; annual for root material (per our compliance).

A few attachments: Acme_BYO_requirements.pdf (detailed controls) and a quick spreadsheet with allowed IP ranges. We’re particularly worried about two items: operator-initiated key escrow and telemetry leakage. Can you provide an architecture note that covers:

1) How customer keys are wrapped and kept opaque to Redwood runtime.
2) Network egress minimization — required control-plane calls vs optional telemetry.
3) Operator access model for on-prem HSMs (what privileges, audit logs, and kill-switches look like).

Would prefer a short written reply and then a 30-minute runbook review call this week if possible.

Thanks,

Jane Doe
Sr. Cloud Security Engineer
Acme Corp

What we will produce (short note + runbook):

Owners:

Two clarifying questions before we write the detailed architecture:
1) For operator access: do you require the ability to remotely apply emergency key unseal, or must all unseal operations be physically on-prem with a local operator?
2) For telemetry: do you accept purely hashed/aggregated runtime telemetry to a vendor endpoint, or must telemetry remain on-prem with manual upload?

Thanks Karthik — quick answers inline to your two clarifying questions, and a couple of preferences:

1) Operator access: Acme policy prefers that unseal operations require a local operator in the customer site. Remote emergency unseal is allowed only if the vendor can provide strong multi-party authorization (M-of-N) with hardware-backed attestations and a post-facto audit.

2) Telemetry: preference is on-prem telemetry processing with an opt-in, push model for aggregated metrics only (no raw logs). If Redwood requires runtime telemetry for performance safety, it must be rate-limited, hashed, and have an opt-out toggle.

Two additional questions for your architects:
- Can you describe the wrapping hierarchy you propose? We want to ensure that even if a vendor control plane is compromised, raw customer secrets are unreachable.
- For rotation automation: how do you handle in-flight sessions/kv-cache when KEKs rotate? We need non-disruptive behavior.

Happy to take the 11:00 PT Tue slot you suggested — please send an invite.

Best,
Jane

Jane / Acme team — thanks for the quick clarifications on operator and telemetry preferences. Attached are two artifacts: BYO-egress-minimization-checklist.xlsx (working spreadsheet) and operator-ops-constraints.md (notes + minimal roles). Highlights and committed actions: 

Highlights (short):
- Sealed-wrap proposal: local HSM retains root key material. Runtime instances receive ephemeral wrapping keys that are session-limited and derived via an HSM-backed blind-wrap protocol. Vendor runtime never has access to unwrapped key material. Diagram in operator-ops-constraints.md shows the M-of-N unseal path for emergency access.
- Egress matrix: control-plane (config fetch + health pings) is required. Optional telemetry entirely opt-in; when enabled it sends hashed counters only to a fixed telemetry endpoint; default is off.
- Rotation behavior: KEK rollover is coordinated via a double-write approach for a 24-hour handover window: new keys are staged, active session tokens use the old wrapped KEK until they expire (TTL configurable), then cleanup occurs. This preserves in-flight KV cache while allowing atomic switch.
- Operator model: local unseal only by customer operators. Vendor can hold sealed backup artifacts (sealed with customer KEK) but only accessible via M-of-N with attested operators and documented manifest. All operator actions write to immutable audit logs (syslog + signed ledger entry).

Action items & owners (by date):
- Karthik: draft formal architecture note and sequence diagrams (due 2026-10-22).
- Monica: produce final egress ACL template and CIDR list for the runbook (due 2026-10-21).
- Mina: confirm audit retention settings and SIEM integration checklist (due 2026-10-22).
- Ben: schedule runbook rehearsal and invite Acme operators (target 2026-10-27).

Attachments: BYO-egress-minimization-checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet, 12KB), operator-ops-constraints.md (text, 4KB)

If any of the owners above need to shift due dates, flag in-thread and we’ll re-sync. Karthik will circulate the runbook draft by COB 10/22 and include the sequence diagram for the blind-wrap protocol.

Thanks — see you on the call.
